turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning. Quick heads-up — I pointed DNS at the new cluster last night before it was fully ready. My bad.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Wait, what? You did what? The new cluster wasn't even passing its readiness probes yet.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, I know. I got impatient. Traffic hit it and it couldn't serve anything — total black hole.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: How long did that last?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hours. And it hit every region, not just one. Global outage, basically.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Ouch. That's the kind of thing that gets you a pager at 3am. What's the fix?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I'm going to wait for the cluster health check before switching DNS next time. Simple, right?

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Sure, as long as you actually remember to do that. But let's talk about the CI thing too — I saw you skipped the flaky tests to make it green.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, they were flaky, I didn't want to block the release. But I'm worried a regression might have slipped into production because of that.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: We'll find out soon enough. Let's just hope it's not another global incident.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Hey, so the regression you were worried about? It did slip into production. The flaky test skip bit us.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Damn. I knew it. Okay, I ran the full regression suite before this release — all of it, no skips.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. And did it catch anything?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, two regressions were caught before shipping. We fixed them and re-ran everything. Clean now.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's the right process. Also, how's the DNS thing going? Did you wait for the health check this time?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I did. Traffic moved over without a hitch. No outage, no drama.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Nice. So we're good now? Just remember to keep doing that.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, I'll just make sure I always wait. It's a discipline thing.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey, I need to tell you something about the DNS failover approach.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: What happened? Did we have another outage?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: No, not yet. But I realized that waiting for the cluster health check before switching DNS — that wasn't enough. It turns out that was wrong.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: What do you mean? It worked last week.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: It worked because I happened to remember. But it's a manual step. If I'm tired, or distracted, or someone else does the switch, they might skip it. And then we're back to the same global outage.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: So what did you do?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I replaced the manual wait with automated health-check-gated DNS failover. The DNS won't even point to a cluster unless the health check passes — and if the cluster dies, traffic auto-routes away from it.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's a big upgrade. So no human can skip the wait anymore?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Exactly. The system enforces it. I was wrong to think 'just wait' was a fix — it's only a fix if you never forget. Now it's built in.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. That's the kind of thing that actually prevents the next incident. And the regression suite — you're keeping that strict too?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, no more skipping flaky tests. Full suite every time. Learned that lesson the hard way.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Sounds like we're finally in a good place.
